specs.parent_req_text: Loom must expose a local read-only web surface for browsing the store without CLI knowledge.

specs.parent_req_text: Loom must capture requirements from chat as they emerge, without the user having to invoke a CLI command for each one.
specs.description: `hooks/loom_intake.py` registers as a UserPromptSubmit hook in `.claude/settings.json`. On each user message it (1) calls a classifier prompt to decide if the message is requirement-shape, (2) runs `services.find_related_requirements` to surface semantic neighbors, and (3) routes through a six-branch decision tree implemented in `src/loom/intake.py`: auto_link, propose, captured_with_rationale, rationale_needed, duplicate, noop. When a capture occurs it calls `services.extract` with `rationale_links=[...]` derived from the related-req hits. Three guardrails gate auto-capture: softener detection (regex on hedge phrases like 'maybe we should'), domain whitelist (only known req domains can auto-link), and a daily auto-link budget (default 5 per project per UTC day). Every fire appends a JSON line to `<project>/.intake-log.jsonl` for `loom intake-stats`. The hook injects a `<system-reminder>` describing the action taken so the agent sees what was captured.
acceptance_criteria: Given a softener-prefixed message ('maybe we should add X'), the hook routes to noop and writes a log line with branch='noop' and reason='softener'

Given a clearly novel requirement-shape message in a whitelisted domain, the hook calls services.extract and writes a Requirement row plus a log line with branch='captured_with_rationale' when neighbors exist
After 5 auto_link branches in one UTC day, the 6th eligible message routes to 'propose' instead and the log records reason='budget_exhausted'
Every fire produces exactly one line in .intake-log.jsonl with keys {ts, branch, classifier_score, related_ids, reason}
loom intake-stats --json aggregates the log by branch and matches a direct line count

specs.parent_req_text: Intake auto-capture must not pollute the store with non-requirement chatter even when the surface signal looks requirement-shaped.
specs.description: Add four lexical screens to `src/loom/intake.py` that run before the LLM classifier and short-circuit to noop. (1) session-scoped phrases: regex match on 'for this session', 'just for now', 'in this conversation'. (2) scenario-paste: detect copy-pasted scenario blocks via fenced code blocks containing 'Given/When/Then' or bullet sequences >5 lines. (3) tool-docs: detect messages that quote tool/API documentation via presence of `function_name(...)` plus 'returns' or 'parameter' tokens. (4) speculation: regex match on 'what if', 'suppose', 'hypothetically'. Each screen records its hit in the intake log under reason='screen:<name>'. Screens were calibrated on the dogfooding audit corpus where unscreened precision was 55%; post-screen precision is 100% on that corpus.
acceptance_criteria: A message containing 'for this session let's use TypeScript' routes to noop with reason='screen:session_scoped'
A pasted 5+ line Given/When/Then block routes to noop with reason='screen:scenario_paste'
On the M14 audit corpus (committed under experiments/), precision is 100% (zero false-capture)
Each screen is independently unit-tested in tests/test_intake_screens.py with at least 3 positive and 3 negative cases
Screens run before the classifier prompt (verifiable by classifier_score absent in log when screen fires)

specs.parent_req_text: A requirement must move through a well-defined lifecycle so reviewers can tell at a glance whether work on it is started, shipped, or stable.
specs.description: Define a strict transition graph on `Requirement.status` enforced in `src/loom/store.py::update_requirement_status`: pending → in_progress → implemented → verified. Superseded and archived are terminal sinks reachable from any state. Illegal transitions raise ValueError with the attempted edge. `services.link()` auto-advances pending → in_progress on first linked Implementation. `services.verify()` advances in_progress → implemented when at least one linked test spec passes. `loom verify-stable --apply` promotes implemented → verified when the requirement has been drift-free for N days (default 14, env `LOOM_VERIFY_STABLE_DAYS`). All transitions append an event to `.loom-events.jsonl` with event_type='status_change' and {from, to, trigger}.
acceptance_criteria: update_requirement_status(req, 'verified') from 'pending' raises ValueError naming the illegal edge
Calling services.link on a pending req with a valid file advances its status to 'in_progress' and writes a status_change event
loom verify-stable --apply on a 20-day drift-free implemented req promotes to verified; the same call on a 5-day req leaves status unchanged
Setting LOOM_VERIFY_STABLE_DAYS=3 changes the threshold (verifiable in tests with monkeypatched env)
Supersede and archive are reachable from every non-terminal state

The PreToolUse hook (`hooks/loom_pretool.py`) extracts the edited line range from Edit/MultiEdit `tool_input` payloads (parsing `old_string` line counts vs file position) and appends it to `.hook-log.jsonl` under key `edited_range`. `loom link` accepts `--lines START-END` to set the range explicitly; without it, the range is inferred from the symbol indexer when available.

specs.parent_req_text: Loom must extract semantic structure from Python source files so it can detect structural drift and feed symbol-level context to executors.
specs.description: Add `src/loom/indexers_py.py` defining `PyIndexer(root: Path)` implementing the `SemanticIndexer` interface from `src/loom/indexers.py` (`symbols_in(path) -> list[Symbol]`, `name_at(path, line, col) -> str | None`, `start()`, `stop()`). Internally it spawns a python-lsp-server subprocess via `subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, '-m', 'pylsp'])` and speaks LSP over stdio using the same JSON-RPC framing as `JsIndexer`. Because pylsp returns `character=0` for document symbols, `_refine_position_to_name(path, line, col, name)` reads the source line and shifts the column to the first occurrence of `name` on that line. Registered with `loom.indexers.register(PyIndexer(root=...))` — opt-in, not auto-loaded.
acceptance_criteria: PyIndexer.symbols_in('src/loom/store.py') returns symbols including 'LoomStore' with a column index pointing at the 'L' of 'LoomStore' (not column 0)
PyIndexer subclasses or matches the SemanticIndexer Protocol — verifiable via isinstance/runtime_checkable check
Spawning uses sys.executable (not bare 'python') so it works inside virtualenvs
Indexer.stop() terminates the pylsp subprocess within 2s; verifiable by polling Popen.poll()
_refine_position_to_name returns the column of 'foo' for a line like '    def foo(self):' when called with name='foo'

specs.parent_req_text: When code is removed or a requirement is retired, Loom must give the user a clear path to clean up the stale links it created.

loom supersede REQ-X on a req linked to 3 files prints exactly 3 cleanup suggestion lines, one per file
Each unlink writes one event to .loom-events.jsonl with event_type='unlink' and {path, req_id, removed_count}

specs.parent_req_text: Teams must be able to share Loom state through git without leaking embedding blobs or audit logs, and must get a byte-deterministic round-trip.
specs.description: Implement `services.export_store(store, out_dir)` and `services.import_store(store, in_dir, policy)`. Export writes one `.jsonl` file per entity kind (`requirements.jsonl`, `specifications.jsonl`, `patterns.jsonl`, `implementations.jsonl`, `tasks.jsonl`) to `<repo>/.loom/`. Each file is sorted by `id`, fields appear in a canonical key order, and lines end with `\n` (LF) regardless of host OS. Embeddings, audit logs (`.loom-events.jsonl`), `Requirement.last_referenced`, and `Implementation.content` are excluded. Import materializes each row into the local store and rebuilds embeddings via the configured provider. Policy: default `error` if local-only rows exist; `--force` drops local extras; `--merge` keeps them. `loom export` and `loom import` are the CLI surfaces.
acceptance_criteria: export then import then export of the same store produces byte-identical .loom/*.jsonl files (verifiable with sha256)

specs.description: The `TestSpecStore` class provides a contract for managing test specifications linked to requirements, exposing methods to add, retrieve, and verify specs via `add_spec`, `get_spec`, and `mark_verified`. It guarantees data persistence by serializing the internal `_specs` dictionary to a JSON file at `.loom-specs.json` and handles private requirement filtering through the `is_private` check against the `PRIVATE.md` list. The store ensures that every stored `TestSpec` object maintains its `req_id` and `last_verified` timestamp, providing a reliable audit trail for requirement compliance.
